description: Inventory Predictor - forecasting methods, model selection, reorder policy and stock health thresholds. Every value here is read through app/modules/inventory/thresholds.py, so retuning the predictor is a JSON edit rather than a code change.

period.description: How the engine turns dated rows into evenly spaced periods. The frequency is inferred from the median gap between consecutive dates in each series and then matched to the closest entry in 'frequencies'.

forecast.description: Horizon and interval settings applied to every series.

simple_moving_average.label: Simple moving average
assumptions: Demand has no trend and no season: the best estimate of the future is the recent average.
Every period inside the window counts equally.
The forecast is flat across the whole horizon.
The prediction interval does not widen with the horizon, because the method assumes a stationary level.

weighted_moving_average.label: Weighted moving average
assumptions: Demand has no trend and no season, but recent periods say more about the future than older ones.
Weights are applied most-recent-first and are normalised to sum to 1.
The forecast is flat across the whole horizon.
The prediction interval does not widen with the horizon, because the method assumes a stationary level.

simple_exponential_smoothing.label: Simple exponential smoothing
assumptions: Demand moves around a level that drifts slowly; there is no systematic trend or season.
Every past period contributes, with a weight that decays geometrically at rate (1 - alpha).
The forecast is flat across the whole horizon and equals the final smoothed level.
The prediction interval widens with the horizon following the standard sqrt(1 + (h-1)*alpha^2) rule.

holt_linear_trend.label: Holt linear trend
assumptions: Demand has a local level and a local trend, both of which drift.
The trend continues linearly across the horizon, multiplied by the damping factor each period.
No seasonal pattern is modelled.
The prediction interval widens with the horizon because level and trend errors accumulate.

holt_winters_seasonal.label: Holt-Winters additive seasonal
assumptions: Demand has a level, a trend and a repeating seasonal pattern of fixed length.
The seasonal effect is additive: it adds or subtracts a quantity, it does not scale demand.
The season repeats unchanged into the future.
At least two complete seasons of history are required, otherwise the method is not offered at all.

The history must also show a measurable repeating shape: the position in the season has to explain at least min_seasonal_strength of the variation in demand, after paying for every seasonal factor being fitted. Below that the method is not offered, because fitting a season to noise produces a confident and wrong forecast.

selection.description: Automatic model selection. Every eligible method is refitted on a shortened history and scored on the SAME held-out periods, so the winner is chosen on data it did not see and the candidates are comparable. complexity_margin_pct charges a model with more smoothing constants for its extra freedom: it only wins if it beats the best simpler model by that margin, because a short backtest is a noisy measurement and the most flexible model wins coin flips it does not deserve.

intermittent.description: Syntetos-Boylan style classification of sparse demand. Trend and seasonal models are not offered for intermittent series, because a run of zeros makes both of them fit noise.

reorder.description: Reorder policy. Safety stock covers demand variability over the lead time at the configured service level; the reorder point is the demand expected during the lead time plus that safety stock.

stock_health.description: Thresholds for overstock, slow-moving and dead-stock classification. Turnover is annualised: total demand over the last year of periods divided by the average stock held.

data_quality.description: What the loader and the engine warn about. None of these stop an analysis - each one becomes a reported warning on the affected series.

reporting.forecast_disclaimer: Demand forecasts, projected stock levels, shortage dates, reorder recommendations and safety-stock figures are statistical estimates calculated from the uploaded history using the documented models and thresholds. They are planning indications, not commitments or guaranteed outcomes. This application is not connected to a live SAP system and no figure here has been validated in a live SAP environment. Any AI generated text explains these numbers and never produces them.
